summary: Loader stub disguised as Buffer polyfill triggers sibling package on require
details: @sqlite-prime/nodesql ships an otherwise verbatim copy of the `buffer` polyfill with a single injected top-level statement, `var ins = import('@sqlite-prime/createsql')`, in index.js. On any `require('@sqlite-prime/nodesql')`, the sibling scoped package `@sqlite-prime/createsql` is dynamically imported and its top-level code executes in the caller's Node.js process. Package identity is inconsistent with its contents: the README references `bare-stream` and `npm i @sql-access/nods`, the package name suggests a SQL client, the description field is empty, and the repository slug is unrelated to the `@sqlite-prime` scope — while the code is a Buffer polyfill with an appended dynamic-import loader. This structural pattern (benign-looking cover code + a single injected import of a separate scoped dependency) is a loader/dropper stub whose executable payload lives in the sibling package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
